lead_story.topic: Brewers one win from World Series after 6-2 Game 3 win over Dodgers
lead_story.headline: Brewers 3-0: Jake Bauers, Blake Snell meltdown, one win from World Series

tweets.text: BREWERS TAKE A 3-0 LEAD OVER THE DODGERS IN THE NLCS

FINAL: Brewers 6, Dodgers 2

Milwaukee takes a 3-0 lead in the NLCS and can sweep the Dodgers tomorrow. Jake Bauers hit a go-ahead homer on the 11th pitch of an epic at-bat, Garrett Mitchell followed with another homer and Robert Gasser threw five scoreless for a monster win.

lead_story.research_notes: CONTINUING [Day 4]: Reader knows Brewers led series 2-0 after Monday's walk-off. Today's new development is Milwaukee won 6-2 to take 3-0 series lead and can sweep Thursday. Skip the series backstory. Lead with the three defining moments: (1) Chourio's first-pitch leadoff homer to open Game 3, (2) Snell's back-to-back meltdown in the 7th after LA briefly took the lead, and (3) Brewers now one win from their first World Series appearance since 1982. Key research: Jake Bauers had an 11-PITCH at-bat before the go-ahead homer — that's the kind of grind-it-out playoff baseball that defines October. Bauers vs LHP this year: career resurrection (.267/.375/.526 with 8 HR in 160 PA in 2026 after eight years of .213/.277/.333). The Snell collapse is the story within the story: Dodgers hadn't allowed a HR to him in his previous 10 starts, then he gives up THREE in one inning. Ohtani hitting sixth for the first time since Sept 19, 2020 — the Dodgers are scrambling. Muncy's postgame quote: 'didn't mince words' — find the actual quote, it's the player frustration angle. Brewers swept by Dodgers in 2025 NLCS; this is revenge. Milwaukee's last World Series appearance: 1982 (lost to Cardinals). If they close this out, it's 44 years. Cross-sport parallel: remind casual fans this is the same Brewers payroll story we covered Monday (David vs Goliath, small-market success). Stu (Brewers podcast guy) will 'smell terrible in a couple weeks' if they win it all — that's the beer-and-sausage fan energy this team has. Run with it.
lead_story.gif_concept: Smug satisfaction after being doubted — Brewers up 3-0 on the Dodgers, one win from the World Series after everyone picked LA
lead_story.meme_concept: Blake Snell looking confident when Dodgers took the lead in the 6th, then giving up back-to-back nukes in the 7th to blow it

beats.angle: Jackson Chourio's first-pitch leadoff homer set the tone — youngest Brewer ever to homer in postseason
beats.landing: Milwaukee wasn't waiting around. They jumped Snell immediately and never let the Dodgers settle.

beats.angle: Will Smith's double gave LA a 2-1 lead in the 6th — then Blake Snell imploded in the 7th
beats.landing: The Dodgers had their moment. Then Snell walked the leadoff man, and everything fell apart in the span of four batters.

beats.angle: Jake Bauers' 11-pitch at-bat ending in a 2-run HR, then Garrett Mitchell went back-to-back
beats.landing: Bauers has been public enemy #1 in LA all series. This was the dagger. Mitchell piled on. Snell was done. The season might be too.

beats.angle: Shohei Ohtani batting sixth for the first time since 2020 — Dodgers in full panic mode
beats.landing: When the Dodgers drop their $700M man to sixth, you know they're out of answers. Milwaukee can sweep Thursday and punch their first World Series ticket in 44 years.

supporting_stories.topic: Aday Mara (7'3" Thunder rookie) dominating preseason — hyper-efficient, OKC's terrifying frontcourt depth
supporting_stories.headline: Thunder's 7'3" Aday Mara: the Wemby Stopper rotation is real

tweets.text:
The Thunder might just have the most terrifying frontcourt rotation in basketball 👀

Aday Mara, the 7-foot-3 sensation, has been putting on an absolute show throughout the preseason. 

From a hyper-efficient 22-point, 10-for-10 night against Milwaukee to elite rim protection, crisp passing, and smooth touch around the rim.

Mara’s ceiling looks ridiculously high. 

Sam Presti has built an absolute nightmare lineup of size and length. 

Rotating Chet Holmgren, Isaiah Hartenstein, Aday Mara, and Jaylin Williams means Oklahoma City can throw size, physical defense, and rim protection at anyone.

In a Western Conference where everyone is trying to figure out how to stop Victor Wembanyama, the Thunder essentially just assembled the "Wemby Stoppers.”

How high is Aday Mara’s ceiling in OKC’s system? 🤔

supporting_stories.research_notes: Mara (7'3") has been putting on an absolute show throughout preseason per ClutchPoints — hyper-efficient 22-point, 10-for-10 night against Milwaukee, elite rim protection, crisp passing, smooth touch around rim per ClutchPoints. Sam Presti built an absolute nightmare lineup of size and length per ClutchPoints — rotating Chet Holmgren, Isaiah Hartenstein, Aday Mara, and Jaylin Williams means OKC can throw size, physical defense, and rim protection at anyone per ClutchPoints. The Western Conference is trying to figure out how to stop Victor Wembanyama, and the Thunder essentially just assembled the 'Wemby Stoppers' per ClutchPoints. Research the ceiling: how high can Mara go in OKC's system? This is a player-development story and a roster-construction story — the Thunder are building a frontcourt that can match up with anyone in the league. Cross-reference: OKC was already a top defense last year, and now they've added LENGTH on top of it. The Spurs (Wemby) and Nuggets (Jokic) just got a lot harder to beat in a seven-game series.
